items.title: Suno lanza un nuevo modelo de IA para música tras múltiples demandas por derechos de autor
Latest Suno lawsuit accuses AI company of violating the publicity rights of musicians rather than infringing their copyrights
items.summary: Suno is facing another lawsuit from the music industry. But this time it’s not a copyright lawsuit. A group of musicians claim Suno has violated their US publicity rights by “encoding musicians’ identities into its AI model” and then “exploiting those identities by publicly using musicians’ names”

items.title: Donald Trump’s DoJ says OpenAI should be able to do whatever it wants with copyright protected works
items.summary: The US Department Of Justice has intervened in a legal battle between the New York Times and OpenAI, arguing that AI training is ‘fair use’ under American copyright law. Whether or not AI training is fair use is at the centre of dozens of AI lawsuits, including those filed by the music industry

items.title: Suno unveils upgrade developed with “music industry partners”, while continuing to battle the music industry in court
items.summary: Suno has unveiled v6 of its music AI platform, which has been developed with its industry partners like Warner Music, BMG and Believe. However, even as it starts to work with some labels and publishers on new AI products, it continues to fight other music companies in the courts

tip.title: Sample sin licencia no se arregla con 'menos de 7 segundos'
tip.body: No existe una cantidad de segundos legalmente segura. Cualquier fragmento reconocible puede ser infracción, y necesitas dos permisos: el de la grabación (sello) y el de la composición (editorial).

tip.title: There is no safe 'under 7 seconds' rule for samples
tip.body: No number of seconds is legally safe. Any recognizable fragment can infringe, and you need two clearances: the master recording (label) and the composition (publisher).
